plan: Second-price auctions reward truthful bidding: your bid determines if you win, not what you pay (you pay the second-highest bid). To maximize expected profit, bid exactly your private value—this sets the correct cutoff where winning is profitable and avoids overpaying if others bid between your value and an inflated bid. With no informative history and one round only, there’s no strategic benefit to shading or bluffing. Therefore, set the bid equal to my value, $25, as my maximum willingness to pay.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is (weakly) dominant. Overbidding risks paying above value if rivals bid near your value; underbidding risks losing when you would have earned positive surplus. With no informative history and only 1 round, there’s no strategic learning or signaling value. Therefore, bid exactly my value: $3.00.
